note: Baseline roster as developed in conversation. Week 1 diffs against this file. scripts/build_report.py copies it to data/sentiment_current.json on first run and updates that file thereafter; this baseline is never overwritten.

fed.name: Fed / Warsh
fed.stance: held 3.75-4.00% on 2026-10-28 (10-2, Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike); statement: inflation 'remains elevated', 'The Committee will deliver price stability'. Barkin and Hammack (11-05) backed gradual increases; Williams (11-06) inflation 'too high for too long'. December hike ~78% priced. October CPI 11-10 is the swing factor
fed.read: policy headwind, tightening bias - hawkish hold, no pivot

roster.name: Yardeni

roster.statement_summary: QuickTakes 'Air Coming Out Of AI Bubble': AI backlash a speed bump, not a roadblock

roster.name: Wood

roster.name: Lee

roster.name: Siegel

roster.name: Sonders
roster.note: Held: mildly constructive; expects rotation and better breadth rather than a broad rally

roster.name: Druckenmiller
roster.note: CUT and GAP CLOSED: reportedly cut AI holdings to ~20% of their level six months earlier (FT, via secondary source), calls AI a likely 'profit bubble' and rates too low

roster.name: Roubini
roster.note: Held: benign baseline, tail risks judged less likely; nothing US-equity specific in the visible text
roster.statement_summary: Project Syndicate 'Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?': markets and economy held up despite tariffs and the energy shock; growth improves in 2027

roster.name: Slok
roster.note: Held: hot PPI plus softer spending is 'the definition of stagflation' and expects data-center build-out to slow, but still no recession

roster.name: El-Erian
roster.note: Held: markets pricing too many hikes; non-tech economy vulnerable to the tech side; AI trade 'has started to realize it's tougher'
roster.statement_summary: CNBC (via Stocktwits): 'I don't think we're going to get three hikes'; low October / high December hike odds about right

roster.name: Gross
roster.note: MOVED CAUTIOUS from neutral: own nothing but 1-year T-bills, be cautious on stocks at record levels because higher yields will compress margins
roster.statement_summary: Investment Outlook / FT op-ed 'Don't own bonds and be cautious with stocks': 'be cautious with stocks at record levels as higher yields over time will contract profit margins'

roster.name: Buffett-Berkshire

roster.name: Marks
roster.note: Held: calls AI 'the least predictable thing I've ever witnessed in my career', can't assess the boom's economic viability - agnostic rather than a new call
roster.statement_summary: CNBC The Exchange: AI is the 'least predictable thing I've ever witnessed'

roster.name: Dimon
roster.note: Held: Q3 call repeats deficits/sticky inflation/high asset prices/rising rates as risks; JPM cut buybacks and is tightening standards on loose leveraged-finance covenants - action now matches rhetoric
roster.statement_summary: JPMorgan Q3 2026 call: 'high asset prices and fairly low credit losses' may not last; tightening lending standards; 'more uncertainty than normal' on 2027 NII

roster.name: Krugman
roster.note: Held: lists triggers for the next slump (stagflation forcing big hikes, AI-bubble bust, debt crisis via long yields) rather than a dated call
roster.statement_summary: Substack 'The Crisis Next Time': a severe slump will eventually come; worried about a liquidity trap if AI capex collapses

roster.name: Dalio

roster.statement_summary: Benzinga: warns of a US debt 'death spiral' as debt and AI equity issuance swamp demand

roster.name: Rosenberg
roster.note: 12m cut -2->-3: calls the US market the 'most stretched' of his 40-year career on valuation, leverage and positioning; shifting to Treasuries and international equities (talk and stated positioning agree)
roster.statement_summary: Bloomberg (via Roic News): 'most stretched' market in four decades, more AI-dependent than tech was pre-dotcom; average S&P stock ~20% below its 52-week high

roster.name: Grantham
roster.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight
roster.statement_summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

roster.name: Burry
roster.note: Held: took profits on 25% of his SMH puts the day SMH fell 11%; remaining June-2027 puts reportedly still large - profit-taking, not a thesis change
roster.statement_summary: Substack 'Trading Post' (reported secondhand): sold 25% of SMH puts, kept the rest, still very bearish
